messages:
tara: Opening a small PR to update the HelloFast quickstart. Plan: prefer REDWOOD_API_KEY env var examples, add devcontainer snippet, and replace `docker run` with `docker compose` for local dev. PR: #4412. Looking for one reviewer.
ben: 👍 Can you paste the concise snippets here so I can sanity-check the code blocks quickly?
ash: Also add a short non-alarming migration note for users of the old SESSION_TOKEN flow.
tara: Paste: 
```bash
# .env
REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_test_ABC123
```
```python
# app.py
import os
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
resp = client.chat.create(model='redwood-mini', input='Hello Quickstart')
print(resp.text)
```

tara: Devcontainer hint: add \"runArgs\": [\"-e\", \"REDWOOD_API_KEY=${localEnv:REDWOOD_API_KEY}\"] to devcontainer.json.
ben: Nice and small. Suggest adding the `docker compose` run command under \"Run locally\": `docker compose up --build hello-fast`.
nash: For migration blurb: \"If you previously used SESSION_TOKEN in examples, set REDWOOD_API_KEY=...; server-side cookie auth remains supported for Dedicated/Private customers (see enterprise auth docs).\" Keep it one sentence.
tara: Added both suggestions and a link-check CI job. Pushed new patch.
link-bot: CI status for PR #4412: lint ok, link-check ok, preview: https://deploy-preview-4412--docs.redwood.ai
ben: LGTM. Approved. I can merge and run a staging smoke deploy.
nash: Approved.
tara: Merged. I'll follow up with a tiny CI smoke that runs the quickstart container and a short migration line into the migration guide. Thanks!
